Department Marketing Statement

Student Health is a full service on campus primary healthcare facility for UCSB students. We see students on both an appointment and walk in basis. Our auxiliary services included on-site laboratory, pharmacy, and x-ray. Our specialty services include psychiatry and sports medicine.

Benefits Of Belonging

Working at UC means being part of this vibrant institution that shines a light on what is possible. People make UC great, and UC recognizes your contributions by making this a great place to work. Excellent retirement and health are just one of the rewards. Learn more about the benefits of working at UC

Brief Summary Of Job Duties

The Transitional Executive Director for Student Health / Assistant Vice Chancellor for Integrated Care (AVC/ED) provides overall strategic and operational leadership for Student Health Services (SHS), driving high-quality, cost-effective care that supports the academic mission and wellbeing of over 25,000 students. The AVC/ED manages daily operations through subordinate managers and senior directors across diverse clinical and administrative disciplines, including primary care, behavioral health, psychiatry, ancillary services, and the Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP). The position holds primary accountability for a $30+ million budget, ~100 FTE staff, regulatory compliance, risk management, and the overall financial, operational, and physical infrastructure of the health system.

Reporting to the Associate Vice Chancellor for Student Wellbeing, this two-year executive appointment provides strategic leadership for implementing organizational improvements identified through a 2026 external review of UC Santa Barbara's Student Health Service and Behavioral Health System of Care planning process. The position leads the development of Student Health's strategic plan, and advances an integrated behavioral health model across Student Health Service, Counseling & Psychological Services, and campus partners, and directs complex organizational change initiatives. Through executive oversight of senior leadership, strategic planning, organizational development, and financial sustainability initiatives, the incumbent is accountable for implementing a coordinated behavioral health system that improves access, care navigation, operational effectiveness, performance outcomes, and long-term organizational sustainability.

Required Qualifications

Master’s degree in Public Health, Healthcare Administration or related fields along with at least 10 years of relevant experience in a leadership or administrative role OR
M.D., Ph.D., Psy.D. or other clinical training along with at least five years of relevant experience in healthcare administration in a leadership role.

Preferred Qualifications

Executive Leadership role in College health care setting.
Experience with physical and psychological health care integration.

Special Conditions Of Employment

This is a two year contract position.
Mandated reporting requirements of Child Abuse
UCSB Campus Security Authority under Clery Act
Works in patient care environment
Satisfactory criminal history background check
UCSB is a Tobacco-Free environment

Misconduct Disclosure Requirement

As a condition of employment, the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.

“Misconduct” Means Any Violation Of The Policies Governing Employee Conduct At The Applicant’s Previous Place Of Employment, Including, But Not Limited To, Violations Of Policies Prohibiting Sexual Harassment, Sexual Assault, Or Other Forms Of Harassment, Or Discrimination, As Defined By The Employer. For Reference, Below Are UC’s Policies Addressing Some Forms Of Misconduct

UC Sexual Violence and Sexual Harassment Policy

UC Anti-Discrimination Policy

Abusive Conduct in the Workplace\

Job Functions And Percentages Of Time

30% Change Management and Organizational Transformation

Strategic Planning & Executive Governance: Directs the Student Health Service executive team in formulating multi-year strategic plans and long-term policies, establishing organizational vision and operational goals that align service delivery with campus needs, care access, and fiscal sustainability.

Operational Transformation & Process Improvement: Exercises high-level administrative authority to execute operational recommendations from the 2026 external review, establishing systems and operational controls to optimize:

Workforce Configuration: Aligning staffing models and FTE allocation with patient demand.
Provider Productivity: Formulating and monitoring daily provider encounter benchmarks.
Billing Expansion & Revenue Optimization: Directing revenue cycle infrastructure and billing team growth.
Coding Education: Overseeing clinical documentation standards and provider feedback loops.

In consultation with the AVC for Student Wellbeing, directs the ongoing rollout of broad report initiatives.

Integrated Care Model Leadership: Provides executive oversight and program evaluation for the large-scale integration and transformation of behavioral health services spanning Student Health Service, Counseling & Psychological Services (CAPS), and campus-wide wellbeing programs. Establishes executive priorities, institutional policy, and implementation frameworks across the Wellbeing Cluster to advance an operationalized, student-centered behavioral health system of care.

Change Management & Organizational Alignment: Directs executive change management strategies and organizational design frameworks to foster interdisciplinary collaboration, inter-departmental alignment, and broad adoption of modernized operating models.

Senior Leadership Advisory: Advises Wellbeing Cluster leadership and campus executives on complex, high-stakes organizational change initiatives, ensuring strict compliance with regulatory mandates, risk management standards, and strategic campus priorities.

Resource & Infrastructure Stewardship: Directs the operational, human resource, and financial infrastructure across the cluster, aligning multi-million-dollar budgets and staffing strategies to sustain the integrated health model.

Special Executive Projects: Performs other high-level healthcare administration and policy duties as assigned by the Associate Vice Chancellor for Student Wellbeing.

50% Operational & Strategic Leadership

Strategic Adaptation & Program Evaluation: Analyzes, evaluates, and adapts Student Health Service through subordinate leadership to respond to evolving student healthcare needs, public health challenges, accreditation and licensing requirements, and funding landscapes.

Strategic Planning & Policy Execution: Formulates and executes strategic action plans, establishing the vision, long-term goals, and operational policies needed to address emerging campus health priorities.

Financial Oversight & Resource Optimization: Monitors and directs financial management, healthcare utilization, cost-containment strategies, and overall organizational design for a large, complex health department to ensure long-term fiscal sustainability.

Comprehensive Care Delivery: Holds executive accountability for the delivery of high-quality, accessible primary, behavioral, and ancillary healthcare services to students by organizing and leveraging integrated on- and off-campus health resources. UC SHIP Governance: Exercises executive responsibility for the oversight, financial design, and utilization of the UC Student Health Insurance Plan (UC SHIP), collaborating with local leadership and actively representing the campus on UC Systemwide Advisory Boards and Implementation Teams.

UC Systemwide Alignment & Collaboration: Collaborates with peer UC Student Health Directors to coordinate cross-campus care models, monitor systemwide costs, arrange care reciprocity, and influence university-wide health policies.

Public Relations & Institutional Integrity: Maintains institutional integrity, protects organizational reputation, and leads public health messaging by serving as the approved authority for campus communications, media requests, and community relations.

20% Resource Management

Fiscal Leadership & Budgetary Control: Accountable for managing a $30+ million budget derived from complex, multi-source funding models; leads the preparation, advocacy, and strategic management of short- and long-term financial plans to ensure long-term organizational viability.

Revenue Optimization & Strategic Analysis: Directs the strategic analysis and development of revenue-generating initiatives across Student Health Service and Counseling & Psychological Services, including third-party billing models, behavioral health reimbursement expansion, and clinic operations.

Workforce Strategy & Personnel Management: Directs overarching human resources strategy and workforce planning to adapt to changing operational demands; oversees through subordinate leadership the recruitment, selection, development, and retention of staff in accordance with UC policies and affirmative action goals.

Executive Oversight & Direct Supervision: Manages daily health system operations through the Student Health Management team, providing direct supervision and executive direction to the SHS Interim Director and the Director of Billing and Revenue Cycle.

HR Governance & Labor Relations Compliance: Maintains final departmental authority for SHS human resources decisions, working in close coordination with Student Affairs, HR, and Labor Relations to ensure strict policy adherence and contract compliance across five represented bargaining units.

Other Special Conditions Of Employment

The below licenses, certificates, credentials, bondability, altered work schedules, furloughs, travel, etc. are required for this position:

Satisfactory criminal history background check
Mandated reporting requirements of Child Abuse
Mandated reporting requirements of Dependent Adult Abuse.

Position Overview

SCOPE OF ROLE :

The Director of Development Operations will build and lead the operational infrastructure that enables S:US’s philanthropy program to grow with discipline, accountability, and a strong donor experience. Reporting to the Vice President of Philanthropy, the Director will serve as both a hands-on practitioner and a people leader: personally, driving high-priority systems, reporting, process, and data work while coaching and supervising the Fundraising Database and Administrative Manager.

This role will establish Development Operations from the ground up, translating fundraising strategy into practical systems, standards, workflows, and management tools. The Director will own fundraising CRM governance, currently centered in Raiser’s Edge, while helping prepare the department for future technology decisions, including a potential transition to Salesforce or another enterprise CRM. Core areas of responsibility include data quality, revenue and pipeline reporting, gift administration, prospect and portfolio infrastructure, process documentation, staff training, change management, and cross-functional coordination with Finance, Programs, Marketing and Communications, Information Technology, and organizational leadership.

The successful candidate will combine strategic judgment with a willingness to execute. They will be comfortable designing the future state, setting priorities, and managing change while also building dashboards, improving records, documenting workflows, troubleshooting day-to-day issues, and ensuring essential work is completed accurately and on time.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Build and Lead Development Operations

Create and implement a phased Development Operations roadmap aligned with philanthropy goals and organizational priorities.
Establish clear ownership, service standards, controls, and decision rights for fundraising operations.
Assess existing practices, identify risks and gaps, and build scalable solutions rather than relying on informal or person-dependent processes.
Balance long-term infrastructure building with timely execution of day-to-day operational needs.
Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Vice President of Philanthropy and translate strategy into measurable operating plans.

CRM Governance, Data Quality, and Adoption

Own the overall effectiveness and governance of the fundraising CRM, currently Raiser’s Edge, and other stakeholders as appropriate.
Develop and maintain standards for constituent records, required fields, coding, gift records, actions, opportunities, relationship management, and portfolio tracking.
Lead data-quality efforts, including duplicate management, data hygiene, audits, exception reporting, and ongoing quality-control routines.
Oversee system configuration, integrations, user access, vendor relationships, upgrades, and issue resolution.
Help lead CRM migration readiness efforts, including business requirements, data clean-up, data mapping, documentation, testing, user training, change management, and post-implementation adoption.
Create practical training, documentation, and reinforcement that increase staff confidence, consistency, and adoption.

Gift Administration and Financial Coordination

Oversee accurate and timely gift entry, acknowledgments, pledges, recurring gifts, matching gifts, third-party gifts, sponsorships, grants, restrictions, and adjustments.
Establish and monitor quality controls for gift processing, documentation, receipting, and stewardship handoffs.
Partner closely with Finance to strengthen revenue reconciliation, restricted-gift tracking, audit readiness, and shared definitions and reporting practices.
Develop and maintain gift acceptance and related fundraising policies in coordination with appropriate internal partners.
Ensure exceptions, unusual gifts, and high-risk transactions are escalated and resolved appropriately.

Reporting, Forecasting, and Decision Support

Design and maintain reliable dashboards and recurring reports for revenue, pipeline, forecasting, retention, engagement, activity, data quality, gift processing, and outstanding obligations.
Create consistent definitions, reporting calendars, and quality checks so leaders and fundraisers can trust and act on the data.
Partner with frontline fundraisers to improve pipeline discipline, moves management, next-step tracking, portfolio reviews, and forecasting.
Analyze trends and translate data into concise, decision-ready insights for department and organizational leadership.
Respond to ad hoc reporting and analysis needs while reducing one-off work through repeatable tools and processes.

Prospect, Portfolio, and Fundraising Enablement

Build the operational framework for prospect identification, qualification, assignment, portfolio management, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship tracking.
Create systems that help fundraisers prioritize relationships, document activity, manage follow-up, and identify retention and upgrade opportunities.
Oversee audience segmentation and list preparation for appeals, events, donor communications, and stewardship efforts.
Partner with fundraising, volunteer engagement, and Marketing and Communications colleagues to connect constituent information and improve relationship continuity.

Policies, Processes, and Change Management

Document, improve, and maintain standard operating procedures for core fundraising and administrative workflows.
Lead process-mapping and redesign efforts that clarify roles, reduce duplication, strengthen controls, and improve efficiency.
Build sustainable systems for storing documentation, maintaining institutional knowledge, and reviewing procedures as practices evolve.
Guide teams through change with clear communication, practical training, realistic sequencing, and consistent follow-through.
Lead implementation of recommendations arising from CRM, Salesforce-readiness, and business-process assessments.

Team Leadership and Hands-On Execution

Supervise, coach, and develop the Fundraising Database and Administrative Manager, setting clear priorities, expectations, and measures of success.
Create an effective division of responsibilities while remaining willing to perform essential operational work directly when needed.
Build a culture of service, accuracy, accountability, continuous improvement, and constructive problem-solving.
Manage multiple projects and recurring deadlines, escalate risks early, and keep stakeholders informed.
Participate in special projects and perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

REQUIREMENTS:
At least 7 years of progressively responsible nonprofit development operations, fundraising systems, advancement services, or closely related experience, including significant hands-on responsibility for CRM administration, reporting, and business processes.
Demonstrated experience building or substantially redesigning Development Operations infrastructure, standards, and workflows in an organization with evolving systems and practices.
At least 3 years of staff supervision, coaching, or team leadership experience.
Advanced experience with Raiser’s Edge, Salesforce, or a comparable fundraising/advancement CRM, including data structure, queries, reports, dashboards, quality control, and user adoption.
Experience supporting CRM selection, implementation, migration, or optimization projects
Experience with gift processing, acknowledgments, revenue reconciliation, pipeline reporting, moves management, and fundraising performance reporting.
Strong project and change-management experience, including the ability to move from assessment to implementation.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and comfort learning and managing related fundraising technology.
Effective written and oral communication skills, including the ability to explain technical or process concepts clearly to varied audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Experience in a large, complex nonprofit, social-services, health and human-services, or similarly matrixed organization.
Experience partnering with Finance, Information Technology, Programs, Marketing and Communications, and executive leadership.
Knowledge of fundraising compliance, gift acceptance, restricted gifts, audit support, privacy, and data-governance practices.
Experience with prospect research, wealth screening, digital fundraising platforms, email marketing systems, integrations, and data visualization tools.
Strong analytical judgment, attention to detail, and ability to distinguish immediate operational needs from longer-term infrastructure priorities.
A collaborative, service-oriented leadership style combined with the confidence to set standards, clarify accountability, and drive adoption.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a player-coach: equally comfortable setting direction, developing staff, and completing detailed work.

jobs.description:
About Cresset

Cresset is a firm built by clients, for clients. As an independent, award-winning multi-family office and private investment firm, we are reimagining the way wealth is experienced. Our purpose is to help ensure that both wealth and life are fully optimized**—integrated, intentional, and aligned with each client’s vision of success.

We provide access to the caliber of talent, ideas, and investment opportunities typically available to the largest single-family offices and institutions. Our approach is personalized, entrepreneurial, and client-first.

Cresset was built to endure. We are creating a 100+ year firm—one focused on delivering an exceptional experience, not only for the families we serve but for the team that serves them. Recognized by Barron’s among the nation’s top multi-family offices,* Cresset is guided by long-term relationships, shared success, and a belief that wealth should serve a life well lived.

Job Description

As Cresset continues to grow through acquisitions, lift-outs, strategic hires, and organic expansion, exceptional onboarding and integration has become a core differentiator of our business. The Managing Director, Head of Advisor Transitions & Integration is responsible for overseeing all aspects of advisor and client transitions from initial due diligence through full integration. This leader will define the strategy, operating model, governance, and execution standards that enable Cresset to deliver a seamless experience for incoming advisors, their team, and clients. While this role is highly strategic, it is equally operational. During periods of advisor onboarding and integration, this leader is expected to be fully embedded with incoming teams, working side by side with advisors, internal Cresset subject matter experts, custodians and 3rd party partners to coordinate resources, remove obstacles, and ensure the successful transition of clients and assets.

This is not a role that leads integrations from afar; it requires a leader who is equally comfortable developing enterprise strategy and rolling up their sleeves to execute alongside the business teams. During onboarding, this leader is expected to be physically present with incoming teams for multiple, consecutive weeks. They will work directly alongside Advisory Practice Management Operations, Client Service, Technology, HR, Compliance, Legal, and other business functions to ensure resources are effectively coordinated and issues are identified and resolved quickly so advisors and their team members can remain focused on serving clients. Success requires calm leadership under pressure, sound judgment, and the ability to rapidly prioritize competing demands while maintaining an exceptional advisor and client experience.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as an active partner to Corporate Development and Advisory Leadership during due diligence to assess operational readiness, integration complexity, technology environments, organizational structures, client service models, and transition risks.
Evaluate advisor operating models and identify opportunities to accelerate integration while preserving the elements that make teams successful.
Lead readiness planning by developing preliminary integration strategies, day one operating models, transition timelines, pre-close checklists, break readiness, resource requirements and alignment internally and with partners, and risk mitigation and contingency plans ahead of break.
Quickly build trusted relationships with incoming leadership teams and team members to establish confidence and ensure a seamless transition.
Support late-stage conversations by clearly articulating the integration approach and advisor experience
Identify critical decisions that must be made prior to onboarding and ensure appropriate alignment internally and with incoming team.

Integration Execution & Delivery

Lead day-to-day execution of integration plans post-break, including regular integration meetings / discussions and working sessions to track progress and resolve blockers
Drive coordination across operations, client service, compliance, technology, reporting, finance, and HR
Translate strategic integration plans into detailed workstreams, timelines, and deliverables
Serve as the primary operator ensuring milestones, risks, and dependencies are actively managed
Identify and resolve issues early, pulling in subject matter experts to triage and stabilize and senior leaders as needed to support
Establish clear ownership and accountability across all integration workstreams

Advisor & Client Transition

Own the advisor transition experience from signed agreement through post-integration stabilization.
Serves as the face of Cresset's transition experience for incoming advisors and teams across the following activities: Advisor onboarding strategy, client transition planning, asset migration coordination, custodian conversion planning, communications, readiness and scenario planning, training coordination, service model implementation, and issue escalation and resolution.

Systems & Data Integration

Oversee integration of technology tools (ex. Salesforce, Addepar, custodian platforms, and financial planning)
Coordinate data migration, validation, and reconciliation
Identify and resolve system gaps, inconsistencies, and reporting issues

Investment & Platform Integration

Support review and mapping of portfolios, securities, and alternative assets
Coordinate platform approvals and transitions with investment and operations teams
Address custodial setup, pricing discrepancies, and account structure issues

Process & Playbook Development

Develop and refine integration playbooks and best practices
Conduct post-mortems, document lessons learned and continuously improve workflows
Support scaling the integration function as deal volume grows

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or certifications a plus.
10+ years of experience in financial services, wealth management, or integration-focused roles.
Demonstrated experience leading large-scale advisor transitions, acquisitions, or enterprise integrations within wealth management or financial services.
Comfortable leading highly visible integrations where executive presence, responsiveness, and sound judgment are essential.
Proven ability to remain calm and decisive while managing multiple priorities in rapidly changing environments.
Experience building trust with founders, advisors, and senior executives during periods of significant organizational change.
Willingness to travel extensively in support of acquisitions, lift-outs, advisor transitions, due diligence, and post-close integration activities.

Northfield Mount Hermon (NMH), a coeducational boarding and day school for grades 9 to 12, plus a postgraduate year, in western Massachusetts near the borders of New Hampshire and Vermont, seeks an entrepreneurial and creative leader and manager to serve as Executive Director of NMH Summer Lab and Auxiliary Initiatives.
The Executive Director will lead the continued evolution and growth of NMH’s summer and auxiliary programs, developing innovative ways to extend the school’s educational mission, introduce new audiences to NMH, make thoughtful use of the school’s extraordinary campus and resources, and generate meaningful revenue in support of the institution.

Located on the banks of the Connecticut River on a 746-acre wooded campus in western Massachusetts, NMH is a coeducational, secular boarding school serving 620 students in grades 9 through 12, plus a postgraduate year, from 50 countries and 30 U.S. states. The school offers an advanced educational experience – the College-Model Academic Program – that empowers students to shape deep learning experiences, follow their passions, and balance rigorous academics with wide-ranging artistic and athletic pursuits. The robust curriculum offers more than 160 courses, including signature programs in environmental studies, the humanities, and social entrepreneurship. NMH’s mission to educate students’ heads, hearts, and hands ensures that they possess the skills, resources, and convictions to serve and lead with humanity and purpose.

Reporting to the Head of School, the Executive Director provides strategic, entrepreneurial, financial, and operational leadership for NMH’s portfolio of summer and auxiliary programs. The role carries responsibility for approximately $1.8 million in annual program activity and for the overall profit and loss associated with these programs. The Executive Director will continually assess the performance of current offerings; identify opportunities for growth, improvement, partnership, and new program development; and ensure that NMH’s programs deliver educational value, an exceptional participant experience, and appropriate financial returns to the school.

The Executive Director will also be a member of the broader NMH community. During the academic year, the position will include limited faculty or community responsibilities, which may include advising, dormitory duty, coaching, teaching, or administrative support as appropriate. This connection to the daily life of the school is important: the strongest summer and auxiliary programs will grow from a deep understanding of NMH, its students, its educational philosophy, and the community and culture that distinguish it.

This is a rare opportunity for a creative and commercially-minded educational leader to build something distinctive at one of the country’s leading boarding schools. NMH is looking for someone who can imagine what is possible, determine what is viable, bring people together around a compelling vision, and then execute with excellence. The successful candidate will combine entrepreneurial energy with sound business judgment, strategic thinking with operational discipline, and ambition with a genuine commitment to NMH’s mission and community.

Salary range is $110,000-$125,000 commensurate with experience. NMH offers a generous benefits package as well, including tuition remission and on-campus housing.

GRADE

LOCATION OF POSITION

MDH Developmental Disabilities Administration, Baltimore MD

Main Purpose of Job

Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Secretary for the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), this senior leadership position functions as the Chief Operating Officer. The Chief Operating Officer (COO) serves as a member of the executive leadership team and provides strategic leadership, direction, and oversight for statewide program operations supporting individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. The COO ensures that DDA’s Community Pathways waiver program is person-centered, compliant with federal and State requirements, fiscally sustainable, and aligned with the Administration's strategic priorities.

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) directs the development, implementation, monitoring, and continuous improvement of the Community Pathways waiver program and Title VII State-funded services. The position leads organizational initiatives that enhance program performance, streamline business processes, and strengthen accountability by working very closely with DDA’s CPO and Deputy Secretary. It plans, coordinates, and implements high-priority, cross-cutting policies that advance Maryland’s mission and strategic goals. The position is subject public-facing during the Legislative Session, and fosters a close partnership with other administrations within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), other state agencies, individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families, non-profits, providers, and advocates to ensure program effectiveness and responsiveness to community needs.

Under the direction of the Deputy Secretary for the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), the Chief Operating Officer serves as a senior executive responsible for providing strategic leadership, program oversight, and organizational direction for the Administration. The position advises the Deputy Secretary on complex policy, programmatic, and operational matters; ensures the effective administration of DDA’s Community Pathways waiver program and services; and leads cross-functional initiatives that improve organizational performance, accountability, quality, and customer service. The Chief Operating Officer represents and acts on behalf of the Deputy Secretary, as assigned, to ensure continuity of leadership and decision-making while advancing the mission of the Maryland Department of Health to improve the health, safety, independence, and quality of life of Marylanders with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

Minimum Qualifications

Qualified candidates must possess a Bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited college or university and a minimum of ten years of high-level executive leadership experience within large-scale human services or healthcare environments.

Extensive expertise in Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS), Medicaid waiver administration and developmental disabilities policy is essential. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in managing fiscal resources and grants, directing strategic planning initiatives, and fostering organizational growth and performance excellence while ensuring strict adherence to complex federal and State regulatory frameworks.

Desired Or Preferred Qualifications

The ideal candidate for the Chief Operating Officer role is a distinguished senior executive with a proven track record of driving large-scale organizational transformation, leading complex cross-functional teams, and championing operational excellence at a system-wide level. Beyond the technical requirements, the candidate must possess superior executive leadership, strategic communication, and consensus-building skills, with a steadfast commitment to advancing equity, person-centered services, and transformative innovation. Demonstrated experience engaging with top-level executive leadership, the Governor's Office, the Maryland General Assembly, CMS, provider networks, and advocacy coalitions is essential. This individual will be a visionary, data-driven strategist capable of architecting productive partnerships and synthesizing policy, operations, and fiscal stewardship into a cohesive statewide strategy to improve the quality of life for Marylanders with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

SELECTION PROCESS

This is a Management Service position and serves at the pleasure of the Appointing Authority. A resume must be uploaded to the application. While cover letters are not mandatory, if you choose to include one, please upload it along with your resume as a single file.

Applicants who meet the minimum (and selective) qualifications will be included in further evaluation. The evaluation may be a rating of your application based on your education, training and experience as they relate to the requirements of the position. Therefore, it is essential that you provide complete and accurate information on your application. Please report all related education, experience, dates and hours of work. Clearly indicate your college degree and major on your application, if applicable. For education obtained outside the U.S., any job offer will be contingent on the candidate providing an evaluation for equivalency by a foreign credential evaluation service prior to starting employment (and may be requested prior to interview).

Complete applications must be submitted by the closing date. Information submitted after this date will not be added.

Incorrect application forms will not be accepted. Resumes will not be accepted in lieu of a completed application.

Candidates may remain on the certified eligible list for a period of at least one year. The resulting certified eligible list for this recruitment may be used for similar positions in this or other State agencies.
